title: Englisch 9 Realschule (ZAM Academy)
description: 36 Kernlektionen zu Berufsorientierung, Indien, Australien, digitalen Medien, Sprache und Literatur; vier freiwillige Grammatikergänzungen. 80 gezielte Wiederholungsfragen mit Lektionslinks. Kommunikative Praxis, natürliche Aufnahmen und eigene Recherche zusätzlich üben. Drei freigegebene Altzuordnungen erhalten ihre Lernverläufe; fünf korrigierte oder mehrteilige Altfragen verlassen die aktive Wiederholung ohne Beherrschungsübertrag.

practice_items.question: Which technique helps you find the application deadline quickly?
practice_items.concept: Scanning

options: Scanning
Predicting

practice_items.question: What does a deadline tell an applicant?
practice_items.concept: The latest time by which an application must arrive.
practice_items.sample_solution: A deadline sets the latest arrival time. If an advert says “by Friday at 16:00”, sending the application later misses the deadline.

practice_items.question: Which CV entry gives evidence of teamwork?
practice_items.concept: Organised a stall with classmates

options: Organised a stall with classmates
Describes every family member

practice_items.question: In a CV, what should support a claimed skill?
practice_items.concept: A specific example of something you have done.
practice_items.sample_solution: Support a skill with a concrete activity. For example, “Organised a stall with classmates” gives evidence for teamwork.

Die Lektion erklärt eine hier verwendete Grundlage; die Wiederholung bleibt freiwillig.

practice_items.question: Which sentence links experience to a useful skill?
practice_items.concept: Keeping records taught me to check details.

options: Keeping records taught me to check details.
I am perfect at absolutely everything.

practice_items.question: What should the opening of an application identify?
practice_items.concept: The position or placement you are applying for.
practice_items.sample_solution: Name the position or placement in the opening. For example, “I am applying for the workshop placement advertised on your website.”

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion erklärt eine hier verwendete Grundlage; die Wiederholung bleibt freiwillig.

practice_items.question: What is a useful response when a question is unclear?
practice_items.concept: Could you explain what you mean?

options: Could you explain what you mean?
I will answer a different question.

practice_items.question: Name a polite phrase that gives you thinking time in an interview.
practice_items.concept: Let me think for a moment.
practice_items.sample_solution: “Let me think for a moment” politely asks for time to organise an answer without changing the question.

atoms.title: Listen to a change of plan

practice_items.question: A caller says, “Your appointment was at 09:00. Please arrive at half past ten instead.” What is the new arrival time?
Why repeat a changed appointment time back to the caller?
practice_items.concept: To check that you understood the new time correctly.
practice_items.sample_solution: Repeating the changed time checks shared understanding: “So I should arrive at half past ten, is that right?”

practice_items.question: Which role sells goods to the final customer?
practice_items.concept: Retailer

options: Retailer
Supplier

practice_items.question: Why use “could” in “Automation could reduce mistakes”?
practice_items.concept: It expresses a possibility rather than a guaranteed result.
practice_items.sample_solution: “Could” marks a possible outcome. “Automation could reduce mistakes” leaves open whether it will actually happen.

practice_items.question: In a simplified business calculation, revenue minus costs equals what?
practice_items.concept: Profit

options: Profit
A loan

practice_items.question: What is a share in a company?
practice_items.concept: An ownership interest in that company.
practice_items.sample_solution: A share represents an ownership interest. Buying shares is different from lending money through a loan.

practice_items.question: Which sentence clearly expresses a personal feeling?
practice_items.concept: I felt nervous on my first morning.

options: I felt nervous on my first morning.
The list contained twelve appointments.

practice_items.question: What does reflection add to an experience report?
practice_items.concept: What you learned and what you would change next time.
practice_items.sample_solution: Reflection explains learning and possible improvement: “I learned to check names twice; next time I will prepare a checklist.”

practice_items.question: Which question best helps evaluate a historical account?
practice_items.concept: Whose perspective is represented?

options: Whose perspective is represented?
Does the writer sound very confident?

practice_items.question: In what year did India become independent from British rule?
practice_items.sample_solution: India became independent from British rule in 1947. This date does not mark the beginning of its much longer history.

practice_items.question: Which question avoids making a cultural assumption?
practice_items.concept: Are there any food needs you want us to consider?

options: Are there any food needs you want us to consider?
Do all people from your country eat exactly alike?

practice_items.question: What is a stereotype?
practice_items.concept: An oversimplified belief applied to a whole group.
practice_items.sample_solution: A stereotype treats a whole group as if its members were alike. A person’s name alone does not tell you their beliefs.

practice_items.question: A fictional story contrasts two cousins in India: one has reliable internet, the other has limited access. What can this story establish?
practice_items.concept: It illustrates two different situations.

options: It illustrates two different situations.
It measures every household in India.

practice_items.question: Why is “in this example” useful when discussing a case study?
practice_items.concept: It limits the claim to the evidence actually given.
practice_items.sample_solution: “In this example” restricts the conclusion to the case described. Two fictional cousins cannot establish a result for every household.

practice_items.question: What should guide the selection of information in mediation?
practice_items.concept: The listener’s purpose and needs.

options: The listener’s purpose and needs.
The original order of every sentence.

practice_items.question: How can you mediate a word you do not know in English?
practice_items.concept: Explain its meaning using simpler words.
practice_items.sample_solution: Paraphrase the meaning in simpler words. If “deadline” is unfamiliar, explain it as “the last time you can send it”.

practice_items.question: Fictional rainfall data for North Bay: January 240 mm, July 20 mm. South Bay: January 35 mm, July 70 mm. Which statement is supported?
practice_items.concept: North Bay is wetter in January than July.

options: North Bay is wetter in January than July.
Every Australian place is wetter in January.

practice_items.question: What must you check before interpreting the height of a rainfall bar?
practice_items.concept: The unit and scale shown on the graph.
practice_items.sample_solution: Check both unit and scale. A rainfall bar marked 240 mm must not be read as a temperature or as 240 rainy days.

practice_items.question: Why is “Australia began in 1788” misleading?
practice_items.concept: It erases the much longer history of First Peoples.

options: It erases the much longer history of First Peoples.
It says federation happened in the twentieth century.

practice_items.question: What political milestone does 1901 mark in Australian history?
practice_items.concept: The federation of the Australian colonies.
practice_items.sample_solution: In 1901 the Australian colonies federated. This political milestone is distinct from colonisation and the much earlier history of First Peoples.

practice_items.question: An exchange student writes, “I stood beside the group for a while. I finally sat down with them.” Which inference is supported?
practice_items.concept: The narrator had hesitated before joining others.

options: The narrator had hesitated before joining others.
Every student disliked the exchange programme.

practice_items.question: What should support an inference about a narrator’s feelings?
practice_items.concept: A specific detail or phrase from the text.
practice_items.sample_solution: Use a text detail as evidence and keep the inference tentative: “Finally” can suggest earlier hesitation in a scene about joining others.

practice_items.question: An announcement says, “We planned to meet in Room Four. Please go to Room Seven instead.” Where should the group meet?
practice_items.concept: Room Seven

options: Room Seven
Room Four

practice_items.question: What does “instead” signal in an announcement?
practice_items.concept: A replacement for the previously mentioned arrangement.
practice_items.sample_solution: “Instead” signals a replacement: in “Room Seven instead of Room Four”, the first room named is now the intended destination.

practice_items.question: Before posting an identifiable photo of other people, which action respects their privacy?
practice_items.concept: Ask before posting an identifiable picture.

options: Ask before posting an identifiable picture.
Assume silence always means agreement.

practice_items.question: Why can a group-chat photo reach people outside the group?
practice_items.concept: Members can forward or copy it.
practice_items.sample_solution: Recipients can copy or forward a photo. A group-chat audience therefore does not guarantee that the image stays within that group.

atoms.title: Describe a graphic and question an ad

practice_items.question: A chart counts the preferences of 20 fictional club members: 12 choose repair tips, 5 adverts, 3 news. What limits a claim about young people in general?
practice_items.concept: Only 20 fictional club members were counted.

options: Only 20 fictional club members were counted.
Every young person in the world was counted.

practice_items.question: What is the first thing to establish when describing a survey graphic?
practice_items.concept: What was measured and who was included.
practice_items.sample_solution: Establish what was measured and who was included. A survey of 20 club members describes that group, not all young people.

practice_items.question: Which reply develops the discussion respectfully?
practice_items.concept: I see your point; could we try silent mode?

options: I see your point; could we try silent mode?
Only foolish people disagree with me at all.

practice_items.question: What does turn-taking mean in a discussion?
practice_items.concept: Sharing speaking turns and responding to other speakers.
practice_items.sample_solution: Turn-taking gives others space to speak and responds to their contributions, for example: “I see your point. May I add an example?”

practice_items.question: An advert claims its product improves memory and refers vaguely to “research”. Which step best checks this claim?
practice_items.concept: Find the original study and examine its method.

options: Find the original study and examine its method.
Count how many reposts repeat the same sentence.

practice_items.question: Why are two copies of the same advert not independent evidence?
practice_items.concept: Both repeat the same underlying source.
practice_items.sample_solution: Two reposts may copy one advert, so they do not provide two independent investigations. Trace the claim back to its original evidence.

practice_items.question: A school-computer instruction says, “Save your work, check that the saved file opens, then sign out.” When should the student sign out?
practice_items.concept: After checking that the saved file opens.

options: After checking that the saved file opens.
Before saving any part of the school work.

practice_items.question: What should you preserve especially carefully when mediating instructions?
practice_items.concept: The conditions and order of the required actions.
practice_items.sample_solution: Keep conditions and order intact: “Save, check the file, then sign out” must not become “Sign out before checking”.

atoms.title: Choose a tense for the meaning

practice_items.question: Which form fits a completed visit yesterday: “Alex ___ the shop yesterday”?
practice_items.concept: visited

options: visited
has visited

practice_items.question: Which tense marks an action completed before another past event?
practice_items.concept: Past perfect.
practice_items.sample_solution: Past perfect marks the earlier of two past events: “The bus had left before we arrived.”

practice_items.question: What does “I used to walk to school” usually imply?
practice_items.concept: Walking was a former habit that has changed.

options: Walking was a former habit that has changed.
Walking is only a plan for next Saturday.

practice_items.question: After “did” in “Did you ___ to cycle?”, which form is used?
practice_items.concept: use
practice_items.sample_solution: Use “use” after “did”: “Did you use to cycle?” The past tense is already carried by “did”.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion erklärt eine hier verwendete Grundlage; die Wiederholung bleibt freiwillig.

practice_items.question: Complete: “I am used to ___ early.”
practice_items.concept: getting up

options: getting up
get up

practice_items.question: What does “get used to” express?
practice_items.concept: The process of becoming familiar with something.
practice_items.sample_solution: “Get used to” describes becoming familiar with something: “I am getting used to travelling by bus” describes an ongoing adjustment.

practice_items.question: Reply in agreement to “I cannot swim”:
practice_items.concept: Neither can I.

options: Neither can I.
So can I.

practice_items.question: Which auxiliary completes agreement with “I enjoyed it”: “So ___ I”?
practice_items.concept: did
practice_items.sample_solution: The auxiliary is “did”: “I enjoyed it.” — “So did I.” It matches the simple past in the first statement.

practice_items.question: With backshift, complete “Tom said that he ___ his key” from “I have lost my key”.
practice_items.concept: had lost

options: had lost
has lost

practice_items.question: Must “here” always change to “there” in reported speech?
practice_items.concept: No. It depends on whether the reporting location has changed.
practice_items.sample_solution: No automatic place-word change is required. “Here” can stay “here” if the report is made in the same place.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion erklärt eine hier verwendete Grundlage; die Wiederholung bleibt freiwillig.

practice_items.question: Which reported question has correct word order?
practice_items.concept: She asked where I worked.

options: She asked where I worked.
She asked where did I work.

practice_items.question: Which two linking words can introduce a reported yes/no question?
practice_items.concept: If or whether.
practice_items.sample_solution: Use “if” or “whether”: “She asked if I was ready” and “She asked whether I was ready” both report a yes/no question.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion erklärt eine hier verwendete Grundlage; die Wiederholung bleibt freiwillig.

practice_items.question: Report “Do not open it”: “She told me ___ it.”
practice_items.concept: not to open

options: not to open
not opening

practice_items.question: After “asked” in a reported request, what identifies the recipient?
practice_items.concept: An object such as me, him, her or us.
practice_items.sample_solution: An object identifies the recipient: “She asked me to wait” tells us that I received the request.

practice_items.question: Which word names the person or organisation that offers work: employer, employee or employment?
practice_items.concept: Employer

options: Employer
Employee

practice_items.question: What should you do after guessing a word’s meaning from its prefix?
practice_items.concept: Check the guess against the context and a suitable reference.
practice_items.sample_solution: Treat a prefix as a clue, then verify the meaning in context and a reference. Word parts alone do not guarantee the right interpretation.

practice_items.question: What does “I had my bike repaired” usually mean?
practice_items.concept: I arranged for someone to repair my bike.

options: I arranged for someone to repair my bike.
I certainly repaired the bicycle by myself.

practice_items.question: What does “bear in mind” mean?
practice_items.concept: Remember or take something into account.
practice_items.sample_solution: “Bear in mind” means remember or take into account: “Bear in mind that the front door may be closed.”

practice_items.question: In a story, a narrator first keeps a bag on a spare chair. Later they welcome a classmate. Which action best shows changed behaviour?
practice_items.concept: They move the bag before being asked.

options: They move the bag before being asked.
They keep the chair blocked all lesson.

practice_items.question: Can a first-person narrator directly know every other character’s thoughts?
practice_items.concept: No. Their viewpoint is limited unless the text establishes otherwise.
practice_items.sample_solution: A first-person narrator normally has a limited viewpoint. They can describe another person’s words or actions but cannot automatically know their thoughts.

atoms.title: A play, a conflict, an adaptation

practice_items.question: What distinguishes a play from a short plot synopsis?
practice_items.concept: It presents action through dramatic dialogue and staging.

options: It presents action through dramatic dialogue and staging.
It must report only the summariser’s own school day.

practice_items.question: Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
practice_items.concept: William Shakespeare.
practice_items.sample_solution: William Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet. A synopsis retells its plot; the play itself presents dramatic dialogue and action.

practice_items.question: Which slide best supports a spoken presentation?
practice_items.concept: A few key points and one relevant labelled visual.

options: A few key points and one relevant labelled visual.
A full script in tiny type read without looking up.

practice_items.question: What should you do if you cannot answer a factual follow-up question?
practice_items.concept: Say what you need to check instead of inventing an answer.
practice_items.sample_solution: Acknowledge the limit and explain what you would check: “I do not know that figure yet; I will look for the original report.”

atoms.title: Use a dictionary and check pronunciation

practice_items.question: Which information helps choose between two meanings of a word?
practice_items.concept: The surrounding sentence and the word class.

options: The surrounding sentence and the word class.
Only the first translation listed on the page.

practice_items.question: Why check pronunciation as well as spelling for a word like “record”?
practice_items.concept: The noun and verb can have different stress patterns.
practice_items.sample_solution: “Record” can have different stress as a noun and a verb. Check the pronunciation for the word class used in your sentence.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion erklärt eine hier verwendete Grundlage; die Wiederholung bleibt freiwillig.
Die Lektion erklärt eine hier verwendete Grundlage; die Wiederholung bleibt freiwillig.

practice_items.question: Which feedback gives a clear next step?
practice_items.concept: Check the word order after “she asked where”.

options: Check the word order after “she asked where”.
Everything you wrote is simply terrible.

practice_items.question: What should an error log contain besides an incorrect form?
practice_items.concept: A corrected example and a short explanation of the pattern.
practice_items.sample_solution: Keep the correction and the reason together: an error log can pair a faulty question order with a corrected example and the embedded-clause rule.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion erklärt eine hier verwendete Grundlage; die Wiederholung bleibt freiwillig.
Die Lektion erklärt eine hier verwendete Grundlage; die Wiederholung bleibt freiwillig.

practice_items.question: Which project question is focused enough for a short investigation?
practice_items.concept: How do two repair guides handle the same fault?

options: How do two repair guides handle the same fault?
What is everything that has ever happened online?

practice_items.question: What should you record for a web source used in a school project?
practice_items.concept: Its title, publisher, date and URL.
practice_items.sample_solution: Record title, publisher, date and URL so that the source can be found and assessed later. Keep the relevant passage or page reference too.

practice_items.question: Complete the Type III conditional: “If she had studied harder, she ___ the exam.”
practice_items.concept: would have passed

options: would have passed
would pass

practice_items.question: What time reference does a Type III conditional normally have?
practice_items.concept: An unreal past situation.
practice_items.sample_solution: Type III normally concerns an unreal past: “If she had studied harder, she would have passed” imagines a different earlier outcome.

atoms.title: Keep the tense in a passive sentence

practice_items.question: Keep the tense: What is the passive of “Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet”?
practice_items.concept: Romeo and Juliet was written by Shakespeare

options: Romeo and Juliet was written by Shakespeare
Romeo and Juliet is written by Shakespeare

practice_items.question: Which passive form keeps the ongoing meaning of “are building a bridge”?
practice_items.concept: A bridge is being built.
practice_items.sample_solution: “A bridge is being built” keeps the ongoing present meaning. “Is built” would lose that aspect.

practice_items.question: When may the relative pronoun be omitted in a defining clause?
practice_items.concept: When it is the object of the relative clause.

options: When it is the object of the relative clause.
Whenever it is the subject of the relative clause.

practice_items.question: Does a defining relative clause normally use separating commas?
practice_items.concept: No.
practice_items.sample_solution: No separating commas are normally used: “The student who called is here” identifies which student is meant.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion erklärt eine hier verwendete Grundlage; die Wiederholung bleibt freiwillig.

practice_items.question: Which word can express possession in a non-defining relative clause?
practice_items.concept: whose

options: whose
that

practice_items.question: Can “that” introduce a non-defining relative clause?
practice_items.concept: No. Use a suitable relative word and keep the separating commas.
practice_items.sample_solution: No. “That” cannot introduce this kind of extra information. For example, “Sam, whose bike was stolen, called us” keeps the commas and possession link.

retired_items.reason: Alter Sammelabruf zu drei Bedingungstypen und je einem Beispiel. Neue Karten sind Einzelabrufe; kein sicher gleicher Gesamtumfang auf einer Karte.
Alte Musterlösung vertauscht Subjekt/Objekt und vermischt reine Passivumformung mit Wechsel von Zeitform und Aspekt. Korrigierter Umfang ohne sicheren Beherrschungsübertrag.
Sammelabruf mehrerer Zeit-, Personen- und Ortswechsel; Korrektur mechanischer Ersetzungsregeln. Neue Einzelkarten bilden keinen sicheren Gesamtnachfolger.
Alte Antwort only who or which ist fachlich unvollständig: whose, when und where sind ebenfalls möglich. Korrigierte Regel übernimmt keine Beherrschung.
Alter Sammelabruf und teils falsche Musterlösung (only who or which); neue Einzelabrufe zu Funktion, Besitz, Kommas und Auslassung sind kein sicher gleicher Gesamtumfang.
